_comment: Feed metadata for Preware. Everything here ends up in the .ipk's control
file: the top-level keys become control fields, and `Source` is written
as ONE line of JSON, which is the shape Preware's package model parses
palm-package writes a control with Section: misc, Maintainer: N/A
<nobody@example.com> and Description: 'This is a webOS application.' —
Preware special-cases that nobody@example.com address to hide it, shows the
Description as the package TITLE, and files anything in 'misc' under
'Unsorted'. So the defaults are not merely ugly, they are wrong.
Version, Package, Architecture and Installed-Size are NOT set here: they
come from palm-package and appinfo.json, which stay the single source of
Fields Preware reads out of Source, for reference: Type, Category, Title,
Icon, LastUpdated, Homepage, Filename, Location, License, FullDescription,
PostRemoveFlags. LastUpdated is stamped at build time and must not be set.

Source.Title: Backup and Restore
_MinWebOSVersion: The TouchPad never shipped anything older than 3.0.0, and this replaces
an app that only exists on webOS 3. No MaxWebOSVersion: Preware treats a
package capped at 3.0.5 as incompatible with a CE 3.1 device (see
packageModel.versionIncompatible), and capping it would hide future
updates from exactly the people this is meant to carry forward.
_PostInstallFlags: ls-hubd and mojodb-luna each read their configuration once, at their own
startup. The postinst writes an ls2 role and a db8 admin grant, so
neither takes effect until the device restarts — which is why the very
first install needs one. Preware prompts for the restart when it sees
this flag, so the user is not left to read a README to find that out.
(An upgrade over an existing install does not need it, but Preware has
no separate 'first install only' flag and a redundant restart is far
cheaper than a silently half-working backup.)
Source.FullDescription:
A working Backup and Restore for webOS, storing backups on the device instead of on Palm's servers.

The Backup app that ships on every webOS device still launches, but it cannot work: it was a thin UI over a service that uploaded everything to Palm's cloud, and those servers went dark in 2013. Nothing underneath is broken — every service that participates in backup still answers — so this replaces only the destination.

What it backs up: accounts, contacts and calendar; system settings and preferences; browser data and stored credentials; application data; anything a third-party app registers for itself; and the applications themselves, reinstalled automatically on restore. Optionally your media from /media/internal, as individually selectable categories (off by default, since a local backup lives on the same volume).

Backups go to /media/internal/webos-backups as plain files you can copy off the device over USB. They are content-addressed, so an unchanged file is stored once no matter how many backups reference it.

Backups are not encrypted. This is a deliberate departure from stock. The original encrypted every file with a device key that does not survive a webOS Doctor and does not exist on another device — making the backup unreadable in precisely the two situations you would reach for it. Anyone with access to the device's USB storage can read a backup, so move it somewhere safe if that matters to you.

Install with Preware, not palm-install, and restart the device once afterwards — only Preware runs the postinst as root, and that is what installs the privileged helper the full backup needs. Without it the app runs in a limited mode and says so.
Source.Changelog: 1.1.0: First public release. Local backup and restore, incremental content-addressed storage, application archive and reinstall, selectable media categories, and restore from any backup on the device.
